label: TP
reason: Both alerts are true positives. Alert 1 (java/xss): User input flows through param -> bar (via switch case C/D) -> fileTarget.toString() -> encodeForHTML() -> HTML output. While encodeForHTML() mitigates XSS in the DISPLAYED output, the raw fileTarget.path still contains user-controlled data enabling path traversal. Alert 2 (java/path-injection): Same flow proves user input reaches fileTarget directly. Switch statement with guess='ABC' sets switchTarget='C', routing to bar=param (line 93). Both sinks receive attacker-controllable data.

evidence.note: User input from request.getParameterValues flows through param variable, then to bar via switch statement (case C/D assigns param), then to fileTarget constructor, creating path traversal vulnerability
